text:
Arturs Silovs came to Pittsburgh as a chance at a starting job, and 15 starts in it is going badly. He's 5-9-1 with an .873 save percentage, having allowed 50 goals on shots that would usually produce 46, and he's 76th of 79 goalies in wins added by saves.

The split is telling. On low-danger shots he has been excellent (.985). On medium- and high-danger chances he has given back almost nine goals between them, .657 on the hard ones against a league .685. Those are the saves that change games, and they're why his last five starts sit at minus-5.9 goals saved above expected, including six goals allowed to Boston on Nov. 5 and five to Calgary on Nov. 25.

Some perspective. Last season's minus-12.8 on our scale was worse than this, and Evolving-Hockey had him slightly positive in 2025-26, so the models disagree on who he is. Our talent range sits just under league average. Watch the high-danger number; if it moves toward normal, so does his record.
headline: Silovs is losing the hard saves in Pittsburgh
